candidates.source_name: Comgate a.s. — Pro média (press room, tiskové zprávy + výroční zprávy)
candidates.why_relevant: Official press room of Comgate a.s. (IČ 279 24 505, Hradec Králové), a Czech-licensed European payment institution running one of the largest CZ payment gateways plus ~10k physical terminals. The page carries dated tiskové zprávy as downloadable PDF/DOCX files (tz-2024-11-26.pdf, tz-2024-11-05.docx, tz-2024-06-18.pdf, tz-2024-01-31.pdf, tz-2023-10-24.pdf, tz-2023-04-20.pdf, tz-2023-02-01.pdf) AND a set of downloadable company annual reports (výroční zprávy) covering 2020-2024, plus a press contact and a 'Zmínili se o nás' media-mentions index. This is a rare case of a CZ payment institution publishing both marketing disclosures and statutory annual reports in one place, and the releases reference merchant surveys and e-commerce performance comparisons — i.e. payment-mix and merchant-behaviour signal ahead of bank/regulator reporting.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of /cs/pro-media to enumerate /files/tz-YYYY-MM-DD.(pdf|docx) links and the annual-report links; download and text-extract each new file (PDF text layer + DOCX). Diff on filename date to detect new releases. Low volume, monthly cadence is sufficient.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of comgate.cz (301 -> comgate.eu/cs), then followed the footer 'Pro média' link and fetched it

candidates.source_name: Comgate — Blog o platebních službách (product + case-study blog)
candidates.why_relevant: Comgate's product and merchant-case-study blog. Observed dated posts include 'Dynamické řízení 3D Secure pro více dokončených plateb' (2026-07-29), 'Comgate Web Checkout: Platba kartou v košíku' (2026-05-29), 'Mobilní checkout v aplikaci pro Android a iOS' (2026-05-21) and 'Rok 2025 v Comgate' (2026-01-23), the last of which discusses growth in payment volume and client count. Named merchant case studies (Colours of Ostrava, TASY, Topgal, Pytloun Hotels, Bosonožka, Zdravotní klaun) are direct merchant-win evidence. Useful for tracking checkout-technology roadmap (3DS risk-based routing, in-cart card payment, in-app checkout) and for building a merchant-logo map.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML listing scrape with pagination; capture title, date, slug, body text. Check for an RSS/Atom feed at the blog root first — if present, prefer it. Monthly cadence.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Footer link from comgate.eu/cs homepage fetch

candidates.source_name: GoPay — Tiskové zprávy (press release category on the GoPay blog)
candidates.why_relevant: The actual press-release archive of GoPay, which operates in CZ as 'GoPay Czech odštěpný závod' and is part of the Worldline group. Observed dated releases carry exactly the kind of quantified payments intelligence this cell exists to capture: 'GoPay spouští odložené platby přes Twisto a Skip Pay' (2024-10-29, BNPL rails added to the gateway), 'GoPay spustí odložené platby' (2024-06-05), the Worldline rebrand (2022-11-16), 'GoPay pokračuje v rekordním růstu' (2021-03-17), and the Worldline acquisition (2020-09-09). Stated figures include 'more than 18,000 e-shops' in CZ+SK and a 2025 target of CZK 90 billion transaction volume with double-digit revenue growth. GoPay self-describes as the largest provider of online payments of Czech origin.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the WordPress-style category listing with pagination (/blog/category/tiskove-zpravy/page/N/); try /feed/ on the category URL for an RSS feed first, which would give clean dated items. Extract numeric claims (objem transakcí, počet e-shopů) into a metrics table.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Fetched gopay.com/cs/pro-media, which pointed to the blog category holding the actual releases

candidates.source_name: GoPay — Pro média (press contact + headline metrics)
candidates.why_relevant: GoPay's media landing page. Names the press contact (Jan Vodička, CMO, jan.vodicka@gopay.cz), states 'more than 11 thousand merchants' across Central Europe and annual transaction volume 'in billions of CZK', and lists reference clients (Skylink, Voyo, O2, Kytary.cz, Footshop, Fortuna, Wedos) — a directly usable merchant-win list. It also routes to the case-study archive. Note the merchant-count figure here (11k, Central Europe) differs from the 18k CZ+SK figure in the press releases; that discrepancy is itself worth tracking as a definitional signal.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency snapshot (quarterly) of the page HTML to diff headline metrics and the reference-client list; treat changes in stated merchant counts as a tracked time series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Link from gopay.com/cs/o-nas fetch

candidates.source_name: GoPay — Účetní závěrky 2020-2024 (statutory financial statements, published on O nás)
candidates.why_relevant: GoPay's 'O nás' page publishes downloadable účetní závěrky (financial statements) for 2020-2024 as PDFs served from site.gopaycdn.com, and lays out the ČNB licensing history: 2007 small-scope financial services (poskytování finančních služeb malého rozsahu), 2012 payment-services/EMI-level licence, 2019 PSD2 services. That licence timeline plus the annual financials give a hard, auditable series for revenue and volume on a CZ payment institution that otherwise discloses only marketing numbers. The CZ operating form is an odštěpný závod (branch), which matters for how the statutory filings are structured.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the O nás page for the site.gopaycdn.com/static/layout/about/ucetni-zaverky-*.pdf links (exact numeric filenames must be read off the live page, not guessed), download PDFs and extract the financial tables. Annual cadence, checked each Q2-Q3.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of the GoPay About page

candidates.source_name: ThePay, a.s. — corporate site (thepay.eu, formerly thepay.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, DIČ CZ28135261, Masarykovo náměstí 102/65, Jihlava) is one of the four domestic CZ gateway brands named in this cell. The old thepay.cz domain now 301-redirects to thepay.eu, itself a signal of a CEE-wide repositioning worth noting. Critically, on the pages inspected (homepage, /cs/kontakt/) there is NO blog, novinky or tiskové zprávy section — ThePay's public communications footprint is thin, so intelligence on it must come from statutory filings (Sbírka listin under IČO 28135261) and third-party press rather than from the company itself. Footer routes: /cs/napoveda/, /cs/kontakt/, /cs/pdf-verze/, /cs/partnersky-program-thepay/.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency site snapshot for product/pricing changes; pair with an IČO-keyed pull of ThePay a.s. filings from the Sbírka listin, which is the only reliable financial series for this actor. Also monitor /cs/pdf-verze/ for downloadable documents.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of thepay.cz (301 -> thepay.eu), then followed the contact page

candidates.source_name: PayU Czech — Zprávy a média (CZ newsroom)
candidates.why_relevant: PayU's Czech-language newsroom, self-described as covering 'Novinky z oblasti fintech, e-commerce trendy a rozhovory'. This is the localised counterpart to PayU's global corporate newsroom and the only PayU channel likely to carry CZ-specific merchant wins, local payment-method launches (bank transfers, Google Pay/Apple Pay, BNPL) and CZ e-commerce commentary. PayU has 20+ years in CEE and runs country sites for CZ, PL, HU and RO, so cross-country comparison is possible from a single operator's disclosures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML listing scrape with pagination of /zpravy-a-media/ and /blog/; probe for a WordPress /feed/ endpoint. Mirror the same collector against poland.payu.com / hungary.payu.com / romania.payu.com to get a CEE comparison set.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowballed from corporate.payu.com regional-site list, then fetched czech.payu.com

candidates.source_name: PayU Global (corporate) — Media and press / News
candidates.why_relevant: PayU's group-level newsroom. Observed dated releases: 'PayU GPO optimisation tools fuel merchant growth' (Mar 2025), 'Redefining Peak Sales Days' (Jan 2025), 'PayU GPO integrates with Google Pay' (Dec 2024), and a CRO appointment (Jul 2024). None are CZ-specific, but GPO (Global Payment Organisation) platform announcements propagate into the Czech product set, and 'peak sales day' analyses cover CEE merchant behaviour. Use as the upstream feed for product/rail changes that will surface in CZ. Press enquiries route via /media-and-press/press-enquires/. No RSS feed observed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /media-and-press/ listing and the /news/<slug>/ detail pages; filter for CEE/Czech keywords. Quarterly cadence is adequate given low posting volume.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of corporate.payu.com after /newsroom/ returned 404; followed the media-and-press link

candidates.source_name: Besteron — CZ blog and company page (besteron.com/cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Besteron is a Slovak-licensed payment institution ('Besteron A.S.', approved and regulated by Národná banka Slovenska, permit ODB-6111/2015-7) selling actively into the Czech market — a live example of the SK-licence / CZ-market passporting pattern this cell must track. Company facts observed on /cz/o-nas/: founded 2014, 4 European markets, 6,100+ clients, Tapeon acquisition and Seyfor becoming majority owner in 2021, Slovenia entry 2022, Croatia entry 2025. CZ helpdesk helpdesk@besteron.cz, +420 910 920 720. There is no dedicated press room; the blog and the webinar/academy section (/cz/webinare/) are the communication channels. The Seyfor ownership link is notable — it ties the gateway to a large CZ/SK business-software group.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /cz/blog/ listing plus /cz/o-nas/ snapshot for the client-count and market-count metrics; also collect the SK-language variant of the same site to catch releases published only for the home market. Cross-reference the NBS register for the licence entry (ODB-6111/2015-7).
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of besteron.cz (301 -> besteron.com/cz/), then followed the About page

candidates.source_name: GP webpay (Global Payments Europe, s.r.o.) — Novinky
candidates.why_relevant: MAJOR ACTOR MISSING FROM THE SEED LIST, found by snowballing. GP webpay is operated by Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (V Olšinách 626/80, Praha 10 - Strašnice) and self-describes as 'nejpoužívanější platební brána v českých e-shopech' (the most-used payment gateway in Czech e-shops). It is the gateway sitting behind much of CZ bank card acquiring, so its novinky feed is arguably the single highest-leverage gateway news source in the country for card-acceptance changes, 3DS mandates and scheme rule rollouts. Any CZ payment-gateway landscape that omits GP webpay is structurally incomplete.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /novinky/ listing and article slugs; also snapshot the homepage claim strings (market-position wording changes are a signal). Pair with Global Payments Inc. (NYSE: GPN) investor filings for the Europe/CEE segment view, and with Sbírka listin filings for Global payments Europe, s.r.o.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball — inferred as a missing CZ gateway actor from the cell's actor map and confirmed by direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Twisto — Pro média (press room)
candidates.why_relevant: Twisto is a CZ-licensed payment institution and the BNPL rail now embedded inside CZ gateways (confirmed by GoPay's 2024-10-29 release adding Twisto and Skip Pay as odložené platby). Its press room carries dated releases from 2018 through January 2026 — market expansion (Bulgaria entry Dec 2025), consumer financial-behaviour surveys, product launches and milestones — plus a press kit and press contact pr@twisto.cz. Historical figures observed include 'odložená platba po vyzkoušení' on 'více než 17 tisíc e-shopů' and 600,000 Czech users as of June 2019. Twisto self-describes as the CZ BNPL market leader. Its survey releases are a recurring source of consumer-side payment-behaviour data.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /pro-media listing (deep archive back to 2018 — do a full backfill once, then incremental). Extract survey findings and merchant/user counts into a metrics series. Note the press kit is hosted on Google Drive, which will need separate handling.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball from the GoPay press release naming Twisto as a BNPL partner; confirmed by direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Skip Pay — Pro novináře (press room) + blog
candidates.why_relevant: Skip Pay s.r.o. (IČO 07093331, Výmolova 353/3, Praha 5 - Radlice, registered at the Municipal Court in Prague), formerly MallPay, operating in cooperation with ČSOB. It is the second BNPL rail integrated into CZ gateways alongside Twisto (per GoPay's 2024 release). The 'Pro novináře' page is an explicit press room offering 'kontakty, loga, infografiky i tiskové zprávy na jednom místě', backed by a blog and a podcast archive. The ČSOB link makes it the bank-affiliated counterweight to Twisto and a useful read on how a large CZ bank is positioning in deferred e-commerce payment.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /pro-novinare for release links and /blog with topic filters; the infographics are image assets and will need OCR if their data matters. Monthly cadence.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball from the GoPay press release naming Skip Pay as a BNPL partner; confirmed by direct fetch of skippay.cz

candidates.source_name: Adyen — Press and media
candidates.why_relevant: Adyen's global press hub, one of the three international acceptance players named in this cell. Important caveat found on inspection: the page is a HUB, not an archive — it offers a PR contact, a press kit and an 'In the Media' section of third-party coverage (FT, The Independent, FinTech Magazine), with NO regional filtering for Europe/CEE/Czech Republic and no dated release list. Czech-specific Adyen news is therefore unlikely to appear here and must be sourced from the IR shareholder letters and from CZ trade press. Adyen lists 28 city offices; whether one is in Prague was not established on this page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-priority snapshot of the hub page for the 'In the Media' outbound links (useful as a third-party-coverage pointer); route the real collection effort to investors.adyen.com instead.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of the known Adyen press URL

candidates.source_name: Adyen N.V. — Investor Relations (financials, shareholder letters, earnings)
candidates.why_relevant: Adyen's IR site is where the substantive disclosure lives: semi-annual shareholder letters (an 'H1 2026 Shareholder Letter' was observed at /financials/h1-2026-c2a1a) plus an earnings-call events track (/events/earnings-call-h1-2026) and governance/AGM sections. As a listed acquirer-processor, Adyen publishes processed-volume and regional revenue data on a fixed calendar — the highest-quality quantitative payments disclosure available to this cell, even though CZ is not broken out separately. Use it to bound European e-commerce acceptance growth and to date Adyen's local product rollouts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Calendar-driven collection twice a year around H1 and FY publication; scrape /financials for new letter/report PDF links and /events for the earnings-call calendar. Whether a regional EMEA volume breakout exists was NOT confirmed on the landing page and must be checked inside an actual shareholder letter before relying on it.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Footer link from adyen.com/press-and-media, then direct fetch of investors.adyen.com

candidates.source_name: Stripe — Newsroom
candidates.why_relevant: Stripe's global newsroom, structured as News / Stories / Company Information with releases observed dated through August 2026 (e.g. an AI-infrastructure launch roundup, a Microsoft Copilot partnership, Treasury in Australia, Gartner recognition for Billing). Key negative observation for this cell: the country/language selector lists many European markets (Poland, Austria, Germany...) but NO Czech Republic option was visible, and no cs-localised newsroom or Czech-specific content was found. Stripe's CZ presence therefore has to be tracked through product/docs pages (supported payment methods, local acquiring, CZK settlement) rather than through a local press room.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the newsroom listing and filter for Europe/CEE/CZK/Czech keywords; supplement with change-detection on Stripe's supported-countries and local-payment-method documentation pages, which is where CZ-relevant changes actually surface. No RSS feed was observed.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of the known Stripe newsroom URL

candidates.source_name: Revolut — Newsroom (revolut.com/news)
candidates.why_relevant: Revolut's newsroom is the channel for Revolut Business announcements, including country-level user/merchant milestones that Revolut publishes market by market — Czechia is one of its larger CEE markets and Revolut Business acceptance/merchant-acquiring news would land here. HOWEVER: the fetch returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Per method, this is a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead source — the newsroom is almost certainly live and simply refuses automated agents. Whether a cs-CZ localised newsroom exists could NOT be established and remains an open question.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Requires a browser-based collector (headless browser with realistic headers/TLS fingerprint) rather than a plain HTTP fetcher. Also probe for a cs-CZ localised path and for a separate Revolut Business blog. Re-verify liveness in the deterministic pass before classifying.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of the known Revolut newsroom URL
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP 403 Forbidden returned to the automated fetch; body not retrieved. Treated as bot-defended-but-live, NOT as dead.

candidates.source_name: ČNB — JERRS: Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů
candidates.why_relevant: THE authoritative actor map for this entire cell. JERRS is the Czech National Bank's register of every financial-market entity that received a licence or permission, was registered, notified or entered into a ČNB-maintained list — explicitly including platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz, and (per the licence categories seen on GoPay's site) poskytovatelé platebních služeb malého rozsahu. It is the only complete, regulator-maintained enumeration of who is licensed to acquire and process payments in CZ, and it also captures inbound EEA passporting, which is how SK-licensed Besteron and NL-licensed Adyen legally serve Czech merchants. Every candidate in this slice should be keyed back to its JERRS entry. Contact data for banks/insurers is refreshed quarterly; other subjects update on notification. The live application sits at jerrs.cnb.cz (apl.cnb.cz 301-redirects there) and offers direct subject search plus pre-built category listings.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the WS JERRS SOAP web service (see separate candidate) for machine-readable pulls. Failing that, pull the category listings ('Základní seznamy') from the jerrs.cnb.cz application for the payment-institution and e-money-institution roles and diff monthly to detect new licences, revocations and passporting notifications. Note: the /cs/dohled-financni-trh/seznamy/jerrs/ path WITH a trailing slash returned 404 on fetch — use the no-trailing-slash form or the jerrs.cnb.cz application directly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Direct fetch of cnb.cz seznamy index, then followed to the JERRS application (apl.cnb.cz 301 -> jerrs.cnb.cz)

candidates.source_name: ČNB — WS JERRS (machine-readable web services for the register)
candidates.why_relevant: The programmatic access layer for JERRS, live since 2019-07-01. It exposes three service families: individual subject detail (identifiers, address, authorisation dates, permitted activities, relationships), subject lists by role (analogous to the public listings — this is how you enumerate all platební instituce), and representative relationships. Synchronous XML request/response; WSDL at https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws; WSDL/XSD schemas published (XSD updated 2022-04-21); role, list and activity code tables published as Excel. This turns the CZ payment-institution licence population into a queryable dataset rather than a scraping exercise, and 'permitted activities' codes let you separate pure gateways from full acquirers and e-money issuers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: ACCESS IS GATED: requires a commercial (non-qualified) certificate from a recognised CA (eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum, or an EU-listed provider) plus an electronically signed access request emailed to jerrsws@cnb.cz naming the requestor, contact person, and certificate serial number and issuer. No fee was stated. Budget lead time for the certificate + onboarding. Once provisioned, run a scheduled SOAP pull of the role-based lists for payment/e-money institution roles and diff monthly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Linked from the ČNB seznamy index page; fetched directly
candidates.observed_blocker: Not blocked technically, but access is credential-gated: commercial certificate + signed registration request to jerrsws@cnb.cz.

candidates.source_name: ČNB — Otevřená data (open datasets of regulated entities)
candidates.why_relevant: ČNB's open-data page publishing CSV downloads of regulated-entity lists, served from the JERRS opendata endpoint (observed pattern: https://jerrs.cnb.cz/apljerrsdad/JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N, with JSON schema files alongside each dataset). IMPORTANT LIMITATION FOUND: the datasets actually enumerated on the page were banks and foreign bank branches, směnárny (currency exchange offices), non-bank consumer-credit providers and consumer-credit intermediaries — a payment-institution or e-money-institution CSV was NOT listed. The p_seznam parameter is a list identifier, so a payment-institution list may still be reachable by enumerating it, but that is a hypothesis to test, not an established fact. Licence terms for reuse were not stated on the page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate the JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ p_seznam identifiers to test whether a platební instituce / instituce elektronických peněz list is exposed as CSV; if it is, this becomes the cheapest possible actor-map feed (no certificate needed, unlike WS JERRS). If not, fall back to WS JERRS. Confirm reuse licence with ČNB before redistributing.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Linked from the ČNB seznamy index page; fetched directly

candidates.source_name: Obchodní rejstřík / Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — statutory filings for CZ payment institutions
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech Ministry of Justice public register with company search plus the Sbírka listin (collection of deeds), which is where CZ payment institutions file their výroční zprávy and účetní závěrky as a legal obligation rather than as marketing. This is the only route to comparable, audited financials across the whole cell — critically for actors with NO press room at all, such as ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261), and for entities whose parents publish nothing local, such as Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (GP webpay) and Skip Pay s.r.o. (IČO 07093331). Comgate a.s. is IČ 279 24 505. Related registers on the same platform: insolvency (isir.justice.cz), trust funds (esf.justice.cz) and beneficial owners (esm.justice.cz) — the last of which resolves ultimate ownership behind gateway brands.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Maintain an IČO watchlist for every payment institution in the cell; poll each company's Sbírka listin index for newly filed účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva documents and download the PDFs. Note many filings are scanned images, so OCR will be needed. Annual cadence with a quarterly sweep (filing dates are irregular and often late). NOTE: the fetch of the register landing page did NOT confirm PDF pricing/format details — verify document access is free before building the pipeline.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Inferred from first principles as the statutory-filing venue for the cell's actors, then confirmed by direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Veřejné rejstříky MSp + dataor.justice.cz (open data for register and Sbírka listin)
candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Justice's NEW unified public-register portal (explicitly described as running in 'ověřovací provoz' / test operation, with or.justice.cz, esf.justice.cz and esm.justice.cz still live during the transition). Two things matter for this cell: (1) the migration means any collector built against or.justice.cz URL patterns has a known future breakage, and should be designed to fail over; (2) the portal states that open data of the public register AND of the Sbírka listin are published under Act No. 106/1999 Sb. on a dedicated data portal at dataor.justice.cz — which, if it exposes filing metadata in bulk, is far cheaper than per-company scraping for tracking when payment institutions file their annual reports.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Evaluate dataor.justice.cz for bulk dumps of register + Sbírka listin metadata (format, update cadence, whether document binaries or only metadata). Use it to drive the IČO watchlist rather than polling or.justice.cz per company. Build the collector against the new portal's URL scheme with or.justice.cz as fallback until the transition completes. CAVEAT: dataor.justice.cz itself was NOT directly fetched in this pass — it was named in the portal's own text, so its contents and formats are an unverified hypothesis.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Referenced from or.justice.cz landing page, then fetched the new portal directly; dataor.justice.cz taken from the portal's own text (not fetched)

candidates.source_name: APEK — Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (novinky, studie, seznam členů)
candidates.why_relevant: APEK is the Czech e-commerce association, stating it represents roughly 75% of Czech online retail turnover and uniting the whole ecosystem including payment solution providers. Two distinct uses for this cell: (1) the SEZNAM ČLENŮ at https://www.apek.cz/seznam-clenu is a ready-made actor map that will surface CZ gateways and payment institutions beyond the seed list (this is exactly how gaps like GP webpay or Shoptet Pay get found); (2) its tiskové zprávy and the 'Studie, data a analýzy' programme at data.apek.cz produce the e-commerce-side denominator (online retail turnover, shopping behaviour) against which gateway volume claims can be sanity-checked. Caveat: much of the study material is a member benefit, so full data access may be paywalled/membership-gated.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /seznam-clenu once per quarter and diff to maintain the CZ payments actor map; scrape /novinky-apek for public releases. Probe data.apek.cz to determine what is public vs member-only — do NOT attempt to bypass any membership gate; if the data is valuable, membership is the legitimate route.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Inferred from first principles (who aggregates the merchant side of online payments in CZ), confirmed by direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Shoptet — Tiskové zprávy (largest CZ e-shop platform, payment-adjacent)
candidates.why_relevant: Shoptet is the dominant CZ e-shop platform and (per Lupa.cz, 2021-09-01) launched its own gateway, Shoptet Pay — making it both a distribution channel for every gateway in this cell and a competitor to them. Its press releases carry platform-wide merchant data with clean date-stamped URLs: 25% platform growth in the prior year (2026-02-09), record Black Friday for Shoptet merchants (2025-12-02), consumer-behaviour research (2025-11-18), marketplace/Allegro integration (2026-04-09), online-offline unification (2026-06-01). IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOUND: no payment-method-mix or payment-adoption statistics were present on the press page inspected — the payment-mix hypothesis for this source is unconfirmed and the value is currently in merchant-base growth and seasonal peak data, which is the demand curve gateways sit on.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /tiskove-zpravy/ — slugs are date-prefixed (YYYY-MM-DD-...) which makes incremental collection and chronological ordering trivial. Separately hunt for a Shoptet Pay product/news page, since that is the in-cell payments asset and was not covered by this fetch.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Inferred as the merchant-platform layer above the gateways; confirmed by direct fetch. Shoptet Pay independently corroborated by the Lupa.cz payment-gateway tag.

candidates.source_name: Lupa.cz — téma 'Platební brány' (CZ internet/tech trade press tag)
candidates.why_relevant: A curated Czech-language topic tag dedicated to payment gateways, showing 22 articles. This is a high-value POINTER: it independently surfaced actors and events not in the seed list — 'Pavel Schwarz prodal francouzské Worldline zbytek své platební brány GoPay' (2023-08-11, the completion of the GoPay ownership transfer), 'Shoptet spouští platební bránu Shoptet Pay' (2021-09-01), and 'mPlatby u O2' (2022-10-05, carrier billing). Trade press dates and names deals that company press rooms soft-pedal or omit entirely, and Lupa covers the ownership/consolidation angle that matters most for a landscape map. Newsletter available ('ČLÁNKY DO MAILU', max 2x weekly); no topic-specific RSS was confirmed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the /n/platebni-brany/ tag listing for headline + date + URL only, and store links/metadata rather than full article text (copyright). Probe for /n/platebni-brany/rss or a site-level feed. Use new names appearing in headlines to trigger actor-map expansion. Also worth adding sibling CZ outlets (e-15, CzechCrunch, Měšec.cz, Podnikatel.cz) as parallel tags — not yet inspected in this pass.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Inferred as the CZ trade-press layer for this cell; confirmed by direct fetch of the topic tag

candidates.source_name: Worldline — Investor Relations (parent of GoPay)
candidates.why_relevant: Worldline (Euronext-listed) fully acquired GoPay — the 2020-09-09 GoPay release announced the combination, the 2022-11-16 release confirmed full integration into the Worldline group, and Lupa.cz dated the sale of the founder's remaining stake to 2023-08-11. GoPay's Czech volumes therefore roll up into Worldline's Merchant Services reporting, making Worldline's periodic results the listed-issuer disclosure layer sitting above the largest Czech-origin gateway. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: the fetch of the IR landing page returned essentially no usable content (only a title fragment), so the specific report types, segment/Central-Europe breakdowns and exact report URLs are UNVERIFIED and must be established before this source is relied on.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Re-attempt with a browser-based fetcher (the page appears JS-rendered). Then locate the financial-publications section and collect annual/half-year reports and quarterly revenue releases on the results calendar; grep for Merchant Services segment and any Central Europe / Czech commentary. Do this ONLY after confirming the segment granularity is actually useful — otherwise deprioritise.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowballed from GoPay press releases naming Worldline as acquirer/parent; IR fetch attempted and returned near-empty content
candidates.observed_blocker: Fetch returned only a title fragment ('en | Worldline Global') with no page body — likely client-side rendering rather than an outright block. Not treated as dead.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already fully consumed before this cell's first query was issued. BOTH planned cs and en searches ('ComGate platební brána tisková zpráva objem transakcí', 'GoPay platební brána novinky tiskové zprávy e-shop') returned a budget-exhausted notice and performed no search. All 25 candidates in this slice were therefore discovered by direct WebFetch of hypothesised URLs plus link-following and snowballing, not by search-engine discovery.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero successful WebSearch calls. ~30 WebFetch calls executed instead, of which the large majority returned usable content; discovery proceeded by first-principles URL hypothesis + footer/nav link-following + snowballing from press-release contents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Snowballing from known actors is strong for depth but systematically weak for DISCOVERY of unknown small actors. Long-tail CZ gateways and small e-money institutions that are not linked from any page I fetched are almost certainly missing. The cell should be re-run with search budget available before its coverage is treated as complete.

negative_findings.description: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, Jihlava) — one of the four named domestic gateway brands in this cell — publishes no blog, no novinky and no tiskové zprávy. Both the homepage (thepay.eu, reached via 301 from thepay.cz) and the contact page were inspected; the footer offers only nápověda, kontakt, pdf-verze and partnerský program.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language terms 'novinky' and 'tiskové zprávy' were searched for on the site and are absent. No press contact published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ThePay cannot be tracked via corporate communications at all. Intelligence on this actor must come entirely from statutory filings (Sbírka listin, IČO 28135261) and third-party trade press. Any collection plan that assumes a press-release feed per gateway will silently produce a blind spot on ThePay.

negative_findings.description: Stripe's newsroom country/language selector was inspected and lists numerous European markets (Poland, Austria, Germany and others) but NO Czech Republic option; no cs-localised newsroom or Czech-specific press content was found. Likewise Adyen's press-and-media page has no regional filtering for Europe/CEE/Czech Republic and is a contact/press-kit hub rather than a dated release archive.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of the three named international players (Stripe, Adyen) have NO Czech local press room. The third (Revolut) could not be checked because the newsroom returned HTTP 403.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief assumes 'local press rooms of Adyen, Stripe and Revolut Business' exist. For Adyen and Stripe they do not. Their CZ activity must instead be inferred from product/docs surfaces (supported countries, local payment methods, CZK settlement, local acquiring) and from CZ trade press — a materially different and more fragile collection method than press-release monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Two sources expected to carry payment-mix data did not. (1) Comgate's blog contains product announcements and merchant case studies but NO posts on transaction volumes, instant payments, payment-method mix or e-commerce statistics; the only volume reference found was qualitative, in 'Rok 2025 v Comgate' (2026-01-23), which mentions growth in payment volume and client count without figures. (2) Shoptet's press page carries merchant-base growth and Black Friday data but NO payment-method-mix or online-payment-adoption statistics.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 'gateways publish payment mix' hypothesis is only weakly supported. Hard numbers found across the whole cell were sparse and mostly on About/media pages rather than in releases: Comgate 23k e-shops / 10k terminals / CZK 616.6m registered capital / 80 staff / 20 years; GoPay 18k e-shops CZ+SK, 11k merchants Central Europe, CZK 90bn volume target for 2025; Twisto 17k e-shops and 600k users (2019); Besteron 6,100+ clients.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Instant-payment adoption and payment-method mix — two of the highest-value signals this cell was scoped to reveal — are NOT reliably published by the gateways themselves. Those metrics will have to come from ČNB payment statistics, APEK research, or bank-side reporting, meaning this cell should be treated as an actor/merchant-win/product-roadmap sensor rather than as a payment-mix data source.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB open-data page was inspected specifically for downloadable CSV lists of platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz. The datasets actually enumerated were banks and foreign bank branches, směnárny, non-bank consumer-credit providers and consumer-credit intermediaries. No payment-institution or e-money-institution CSV was listed. Licence terms for reuse were also not stated anywhere on the page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-institution open data not confirmed to exist. The JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N endpoint pattern was observed, so other list ids may exist, but this is an untested hypothesis.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cheap open-data path to the CZ payment-institution actor map is not confirmed. The fallback, WS JERRS, requires a commercial certificate and a signed registration request to jerrsws@cnb.cz — a procurement lead time that should be started early rather than discovered late.

negative_findings.description: https://www.revolut.com/news/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body. Per method this is recorded as a bot-defence hypothesis, NOT as a dead source. Whether Revolut operates a cs-CZ localised newsroom, and whether Revolut Business CZ announcements appear there, could not be determined.
negative_findings.result_summary: One of the three named international press rooms is unreadable by plain HTTP fetch and requires a browser-based collector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Revolut is a significant CZ market participant and Revolut Business is directly in scope for merchant acceptance. Leaving this unresolved is a real coverage hole, and the fix (headless browser) is a different collector class from the rest of this slice.

negative_findings.description: Several hypothesised URLs returned 404 or redirected, and are recorded here so they are not mistaken for dead sources: comgate.cz/blog 301 -> comgate.eu/cs/blog which then 404s (the real blog is /cs/blog-o-platebnich-sluzbach); comgate.eu/cs/zminili-se-o-nas 404s although the pro-media page references a 'Zmínili se o nás' media-mentions page (correct slug unknown); cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/seznamy/jerrs/ (trailing slash) 404s; corporate.payu.com/newsroom/ 404s (correct path is /media-and-press/); thepay.cz 301 -> thepay.eu; besteron.cz 301 -> besteron.com/cz/; apl.cnb.cz 301 -> jerrs.cnb.cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Domain migrations are widespread in this cell — three of the five domestic actors have moved from .cz to .eu/.com domains, and ČNB has moved its register application host.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any historical link list for CZ gateways is likely stale. Collectors must follow redirects and must not treat a 404 on a guessed slug as evidence a section does not exist. The unresolved 'Zmínili se o nás' page in particular is a lost third-party-coverage index for Comgate.

negative_findings.description: IČO/registration identifiers could not be established from the companies' own sites for several in-cell actors: PayU's Czech legal entity name and IČO are absent from czech.payu.com; Besteron's site gives the NBS permit number (ODB-6111/2015-7) and the name 'Besteron A.S.' but no IČO/IČO SK; GoPay's site does not display an IČO for the odštěpný závod. Confirmed identifiers found: Comgate a.s. IČ 279 24 505 / DIČ CZ27924505; ThePay, a.s. IČO 28135261 / DIČ CZ28135261; Skip Pay s.r.o. IČO 07093331; Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (address only).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only 4 of ~8 CZ-relevant entities have a confirmed registration identifier from primary sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The IČO is the join key between the marketing layer (press rooms) and the statutory layer (Sbírka listin, JERRS). Without it, annual reports and licence records cannot be automatically linked to the right brand, and brand-to-entity mapping errors are likely (e.g. GoPay's CZ branch vs its foreign parent).

coverage_gaps.description: No search-engine discovery was possible in this run (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first query). Coverage rests entirely on first-principles URL hypothesis and snowballing, which cannot find actors that no fetched page links to.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with WebSearch budget available, issuing the six seed queries plus the extended cs query set: 'seznam platebních institucí ČNB', 'instituce elektronických peněz Česká republika seznam', 'platební brána pro e-shop srovnání 2026', 'poskytovatel platebních služeb malého rozsahu registrace', 'objem transakcí platební brána Česko miliard korun', 'okamžité platby e-shop platební brána'.

coverage_gaps.description: The seed list omitted GP webpay (Global payments Europe, s.r.o.), which self-describes as the most-used payment gateway in Czech e-shops — found only by snowballing. If the single largest actor was missing from the seeds, other significant actors are probably missing too. Actors identified but NOT yet source-profiled in this pass: Shoptet Pay (launched 2021-09-01 per Lupa.cz), Worldline CZ as a direct entity, Barion, Pays.cz, Fondy, and the meal-voucher/benefit e-money issuers (Pluxee/Sodexo, Edenred, Up Česká republika, Benefit Plus) which are licensed instituce elektronických peněz in scope for the 'e-money institutions' half of this cell but were not investigated at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rebuild the actor map from the authoritative bottom up: pull the full platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz role lists from JERRS/WS JERRS, cross-reference against the APEK seznam členů, and profile every entity that appears in either but not in this slice. Explicitly cover the e-money/benefit-card segment, which is currently at zero coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Instant-payment (okamžité platby) adoption — an explicitly stated goal of this cell — was not evidenced in ANY source inspected. No gateway published instant-payment volume, share or adoption data. Similarly, payment-method mix (card vs bank transfer vs wallet vs BNPL) was absent from every corporate source, including the two most likely candidates (Comgate blog, Shoptet press).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not rely on the gateway layer for these two metrics. Route them to ČNB payment statistics and to APEK's studie/data programme (data.apek.cz), and check whether ČSOB/ČS/KB or the CNB's platební styk statistics publish okamžité platby series. Re-scope this cell's expected output to merchant wins, product/rail roadmap, ownership changes and company-level volume claims.

coverage_gaps.description: Three sources need collection machinery this slice did not establish: Revolut's newsroom (HTTP 403, needs headless browser), Worldline IR (JS-rendered, near-empty response to plain fetch), and WS JERRS (requires a commercial certificate from eIdentity/I.CA/PostSignum plus an electronically signed request to jerrsws@cnb.cz).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a headless-browser collector tier for bot-defended and JS-rendered sources. Separately, start the ČNB WS JERRS certificate procurement now — it has an administrative lead time and gates the single most authoritative actor-map feed for this cell. Test the JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ p_seznam enumeration first, as it may make the certificate unnecessary.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was achieved for the domestic layer — cs terms (platební brána, tisková zpráva, pro média, výroční zpráva, účetní závěrka, obchodní rejstřík, sbírka listin, platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, odložená platba, objem transakcí, zprávy a média, pro novináře) were used throughout and drove most successful discoveries. However, Slovak-language coverage was NOT attempted despite being materially relevant: Besteron is NBS-licensed and passporting into CZ, and GoPay reports CZ+SK merchant counts jointly. Nothing was collected in sk.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Slovak term set (platobná brána, tlačová správa, výročná správa, platobná inštitúcia, inštitúcia elektronických peňazí, Národná banka Slovenska) and cover the NBS register plus the SK-language variants of Besteron and GoPay, since SK-licensed entities serving CZ merchants are otherwise invisible to a cs-only sweep.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one CZ trade-press pointer (Lupa.cz's 'Platební brány' tag, 22 articles) was profiled, and it proved highly productive — it independently dated the GoPay/Worldline ownership completion and surfaced Shoptet Pay. No other Czech outlet was inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile parallel CZ outlets and their payments/fintech topic tags: e15.cz, CzechCrunch, Měšec.cz, Podnikatel.cz, Hospodářské noviny, Forbes CZ, and the specialist banking press. Prefer topic-tag and RSS endpoints over homepage scraping, and store headline+date+URL metadata only, given editorial content is copyrighted.

coverage_gaps.description: Several assertions in this slice are hypotheses carried forward rather than confirmed facts: dataor.justice.cz contents and formats (named in portal text, never fetched); whether or.justice.cz Sbírka listin documents are free PDFs (not confirmed on the landing page); whether Adyen's shareholder letters contain an EMEA/Europe volume breakout (not confirmed on the IR landing page); the exact filenames of GoPay's ucetni-zaverky-*.pdf files (a placeholder pattern was reported, deliberately not guessed); Comgate's 'Zmínili se o nás' correct slug; whether Adyen has a Prague office among its 28 cities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve each of these with a targeted fetch in the next pass before any collector is built on top of them. None should be treated as established. In particular, confirm Sbírka listin document access is free before scoping the statutory-filings pipeline, since that pipeline is the backbone of annual-report coverage for this cell.

brief: Czech online payment acceptance is served by a dense, consolidating layer of payment institutions whose public footprint splits sharply in two: a marketing layer (press rooms, blogs, merchant case studies) that is rich in merchant wins and product roadmap but poor in hard numbers, and a statutory layer (ČNB JERRS licences, Sbírka listin annual reports) that is authoritative but slow. The strongest direct sources are Comgate's Pro média page — unusually publishing both dated tiskové zprávy and 2020-2024 annual reports — GoPay's tiskové zprávy archive (18k e-shops, a stated CZK 90bn 2025 volume target, now inside Worldline), PayU's Czech-language Zprávy a média, and GP webpay, a major gateway absent from the seed list and found only by snowballing. Coverage is uneven at the edges: ThePay publishes nothing at all and is reachable only through its IČO 28135261 filings, Adyen and Stripe have no Czech local press room despite the cell brief assuming one, and Revolut's newsroom is bot-defended (403, presumed live). Two headline expectations for this cell did not survive contact with the evidence — instant-payment adoption and payment-method mix are not published by the gateways themselves and must be sourced from ČNB statistics and APEK research instead, so this cell is best treated as a merchant-win, ownership and product-rail sensor rather than a payments-volume data source.
